title: Frequency of Urination
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with urinary frequency, hesitancy, weak stream, nocturia — similar to BPH. DRE reveals a hard, irregular, nodular prostate (vs smooth and enlarged in BPH). PSA is elevated. Diagnosis: prostate biopsy (transrectal ultrasound-guided — TRUS biopsy). Gleason score from biopsy determines grade. MRI prostate can help identify suspicious lesions. Staging: CT abdomen/pelvis, bone scan (bone mets common). Treatment depends on risk stratification: low-risk → active surveillance. Intermediate/high → radical prostatectomy or radiation therapy (external beam or brachytherapy). Metastatic → androgen deprivation therapy (GnRH agonists, anti-androgens). Most prostate cancers are adenocarcinomas. Screening: PSA screening controversial — shared decision-making.

stacks.label: Refer urology / oncology
stacks.finding: Active surveillance vs surgery vs radiation.
